src/cpu/sse_math.hpp.reason: Narrow typed scalar compatibility API and owned MXCSR/thread binding are legitimate CPU semantics; compact private declarations/legacy enum spelling are nonblocking style cleanup.
src/cpu/sse_math.hpp.semantic_justification: All 180 lines read, including every helper and public method. Scalar arithmetic rounds via integer SoftFloat 8086-SSE entry points, using caller-selected MXCSR. DAZ replaces denormal operands with signed zero before work. NaN priority comes from the SSE specialization, not the x87 propagation owner. ordered() equates both zero signs and reverses negative ordering. COMISS and low-lane signaling less_than flag any NaN; UCOMISD flags signaling NaNs only; MINSS flags NaNs and returns its second operand unchanged, including equal signed zeros and signaling payload. CVTT truncates independently of RC, returns the specialization integer indefinite for invalid inputs, and adds no denormal-operand flag. Binary work gives invalid/divide-by-zero precedence over denormals and traps unmasked denormals before committing later underflow/precision. finish32 and the analogous subtract_double tail implement underflow masking/FTZ signed-zero/status and overflow precision suppression. sqrt_single/sqrt produce non-tiny roots for valid nonzero inputs and do not need a result FTZ pass. commit ORs sticky status first, tests only this operation flags against masks, and throws before destination return; prior unmasked sticky flags alone do not retrap. This is a scalar model: packed instruction lane atomicity is a caller question. No game state, PE read, address dispatch or fixture-availability state is present.

resolved_owners.resolution: Sse32/Sse64 own binary words by value; they are scalar representations, not guest addresses or register files. Each noncopyable SseContext owns mxcsr_ and its construction thread id. Every public access/operation checks thread identity directly or through binary(); no transferable ambient SSE owner exists. Caller must keep the borrowed context alive on that thread. Operation snapshots shared SoftFloat TLS rounding, tininess and flags, installs selected RC/after-rounding/zero flags, then restores all three at normal return and SseError unwinding. It neither reads nor writes extF80_roundingPrecision, so no restoration of that untouched TLS is required. X87Context::Operation separately saves/restores all four TLS values. Shared softfloat_state.c is the sole SoftFloat TLS definition; softfloat_sse adds no state object. Distinct Display, NativeGame, probe and invocation contexts are separate execution worlds, not duplicate source-global ownership. Thread checking is a misuse guard, not synchronization for simultaneous races.

resolved_consumers.resolution: Production Display owns sse_{8064}; Application creates native::Input borrowing display.sse(), with display lifetime covering Input. Native Input::Impl uses the borrowed context in input_mod_on_input -> pad trigger/axes/keyboard conversion. InputState::sample_tick is a separate diagnostic native snapshot policy and also borrows a context. Display/render projection calls flow through ninja_projected_depth and D3DX; native view uses shared D3DX primitives. D3DX implements lane loops and explicit approximate-reciprocal policy (scratch SseContext), so scalar API approval does not approve packed exception/store atomicity or hardware RCP/RSQRT accuracy. Reference NativeGame owns its own persistent context shared across input and projection; override_table and HLE bridge create invocation-local contexts from guest MXCSR. The inspected D3DX overrides publish values but do not write local SSE sticky flags back to guest MXCSR. That adapter status gap is outside these four files and is not fixed or qualified here. crt_floor uses subtract_double/less_than only in its explicit SSE fast path and remains maintained outside the native source list.

src/cpu/crt_sqrt.hpp.reason: CRT entry contract still exposes unavailable source-policy facts/source-PC diagnostics and lacks canonical entry provenance; complete implementation also needs statement layout cleanup.
src/cpu/crt_sqrt.hpp.semantic_justification: All 40 lines read: bits, body, binary64 entry and retained entry. Binary64 entry uses load_crt_binary64_argument: finite FLD64-equivalent, direct ext80 nonfinite construction preserving signaling encoding until source arithmetic. body classifies exponent/fraction/sign, saves CW, installs (saved precision bits)|0x007f for finite inputs unless saved is 0x027f, preserving precision while selecting nearest/masked setup. Quiet NaN returns through error code 7; signaling NaN adds m64 one to quiet/flag via source arithmetic and uses code 1. Negative nonzero, including negative infinity, returns ext80 indefinite/code 1; negative zero and positive infinity bypass FSQRT. Other values use X87Context::sqrt. Retained entry first spills input to binary64 for classification but computes with the original retained ext80 input; spill rounding/flags and nonfinite conversion may occur before body saves CW. This is different from scalar SSE SQRTSD and from Ninja signed-root compare/reload/sign preservation. Replacing any with std::sqrt or sharing a generic root implementation has no proof here. Source policy boundaries 0x6452ce/0x64532b are actual diagnostic PCs, unlike IEEE masks: they are passed as data in game-tier code and lack a semantic/reference mapping. Both entries lack canonical FUNCTION/LIBRARY provenance; ordinary address comments are not annotations.

resolved_owners.resolution: crt_sqrt owns no persistent state. Caller owns X87Context and CrtAsinRuntime; the synchronous CrtInverseFrame borrows both and owns function identity, classified double, saved CW and source-boundary metadata. X87Value is an immutable ext80 value independent of context storage; returned values remain usable with an appropriate live context. finish_crt_inverse in crt_asin.cpp is the one shared asin/acos/sqrt return/error owner. Optional matherr_control represents an unavailable source-runtime word, not actual game absence: this reference knownness enters the public CPU contract. Optional result/pending_stored_result instead describe real computation progress. Missing policy returns a computed ext80 value at the changed source CW; missing/failed handler retains its prior binary64 store and no ext80 destination. Successful bypass/handler reload restores saved CW in source order. CRT intentionally has no outer CW rollback RAII on failure; adding one would erase the current boundary contract. Lower X87 operations still restore SoftFloat TLS on arithmetic throw while retaining context sticky flags.

resolved_consumers.resolution: Actual source consumer crt_sqrt is player_mesh_math::normalize, used by normalize_mesh_vector_zero/up. It retains squared m32 spill and m64 root argument, checks failure before vector writes, performs two root m32 stores, then reciprocal/ordered component publication. MeshMathProbe and mesh unit exercise this contract; broader mesh-query/scene consumers remain maintained, even though player_mesh_math.cpp and crt_sqrt.cpp are absent from native-sources.txt at this base. crt_sqrt_extended has no maintained src call site beyond its declaration/definition in the inspected search; it remains a retained compatibility contract, not obsolete. NinjaLength -> ExactFloat::vector_length_return -> signed_square_root -> X87Context::sqrt bypasses CRT entirely; legacy signed_sqrt_extended also uses raw X87 sqrt. Its shared retained njScalor body is already integrated and must not be mistaken for a duplicate CRT/SSE root owner. CRT shares finish_crt_inverse with asin/acos, so separating unknown-policy diagnostics requires all those consumers to preserve aliases, handler reload, status and failure prefixes together. In player_mesh_query.cpp, normal normalization uses the up fallback and direction normalization uses zero fallback; each forwards the same runtime.inverse_math and propagates the nested CRT boundary before further mesh work.

accepted_judges.limits: No new execution. Unit has no retained-entry case. Mock matherr handler does not establish real CRT dispatcher behavior, unmasked hardware timing or every pending-result failure prefix.

src/cpu/crt_sqrt.semantic_justification: All 40 lines read: bits, body, binary64 entry and retained entry. Binary64 entry uses load_crt_binary64_argument: finite FLD64-equivalent, direct ext80 nonfinite construction preserving signaling encoding until source arithmetic. body classifies exponent/fraction/sign, saves CW, installs (saved precision bits)|0x007f for finite inputs unless saved is 0x027f, preserving precision while selecting nearest/masked setup. Quiet NaN returns through error code 7; signaling NaN adds m64 one to quiet/flag via source arithmetic and uses code 1. Negative nonzero, including negative infinity, returns ext80 indefinite/code 1; negative zero and positive infinity bypass FSQRT. Other values use X87Context::sqrt. Retained entry first spills input to binary64 for classification but computes with the original retained ext80 input; spill rounding/flags and nonfinite conversion may occur before body saves CW. This is different from scalar SSE SQRTSD and from Ninja signed-root compare/reload/sign preservation. Replacing any with std::sqrt or sharing a generic root implementation has no proof here. Source policy boundaries 0x6452ce/0x64532b are actual diagnostic PCs, unlike IEEE masks: they are passed as data in game-tier code and lack a semantic/reference mapping. Both entries lack canonical FUNCTION/LIBRARY provenance; ordinary address comments are not annotations.

resolved_owners.resolution: crt_sqrt owns no persistent state. Caller owns X87Context and CrtAsinRuntime; the synchronous CrtInverseFrame borrows both and owns function identity, classified double, saved CW and source-boundary metadata. X87Value is an immutable ext80 value independent of context storage; returned values remain usable with an appropriate live context. finish_crt_inverse in crt_asin.cpp is the one shared asin/acos/sqrt return/error owner. Optional matherr_control represents an unavailable source-runtime word, not actual game absence: this reference knownness enters the public CPU contract. Optional result/pending_stored_result instead describe real computation progress. Missing policy returns a computed ext80 value at the changed source CW; missing/failed handler retains its prior binary64 store and no ext80 destination. Successful bypass/handler reload restores saved CW in source order. CRT intentionally has no outer CW rollback RAII on failure; adding one would erase the current boundary contract. Lower X87 operations still restore SoftFloat TLS on arithmetic throw while retaining context sticky flags.

resolved_consumers.resolution: Actual source consumer crt_sqrt is player_mesh_math::normalize, used by normalize_mesh_vector_zero/up. It retains squared m32 spill and m64 root argument, checks failure before vector writes, performs two root m32 stores, then reciprocal/ordered component publication. MeshMathProbe and mesh unit exercise this contract; broader mesh-query/scene consumers remain maintained, even though player_mesh_math.cpp and crt_sqrt.cpp are absent from native-sources.txt at this base. crt_sqrt_extended has no maintained src call site beyond its declaration/definition in the inspected search; it remains a retained compatibility contract, not obsolete. NinjaLength -> ExactFloat::vector_length_return -> signed_square_root -> X87Context::sqrt bypasses CRT entirely; legacy signed_sqrt_extended also uses raw X87 sqrt. Its shared retained njScalor body is already integrated and must not be mistaken for a duplicate CRT/SSE root owner. CRT shares finish_crt_inverse with asin/acos, so separating unknown-policy diagnostics requires all those consumers to preserve aliases, handler reload, status and failure prefixes together. In player_mesh_query.cpp, normal normalization uses the up fallback and direction normalization uses zero fallback; each forwards the same runtime.inverse_math and propagates the nested CRT boundary before further mesh work.
